course: Pizza Oven Construction - Wood Fired 12 Pizza

lessons.title: Overview of Wood-Fired Oven Types
lessons.body: Wood-fired pizza ovens come in three main types: brick, cob, and metal. For a 12-inch pizza, you need an oven with a cooking floor of at least 60 cm x 60 cm. In Africa, brick ovens are most common because clay bricks are locally made and cheap. A simple brick oven uses firebricks for the floor (they withstand high heat) and regular clay bricks for the dome. You can build one for about 200 USD if you gather materials yourself. Cob ovens use a mix of clay, sand, and straw. They are cheap (under 100 USD) but crack easily in heavy rain, so they need a roof. Metal ovens are made from steel drums or custom welded boxes. They heat fast but lose heat quickly, so you need more wood. For a beginner, a brick oven with a firebrick floor and a clay dome is best. It holds heat for hours and can bake 12-inch pizzas in 90 seconds. In many African towns, you can find firebricks at building supply stores or pottery factories. If not, use dense clay bricks and line the floor with a layer of sand mixed with clay to protect from thermal shock. The dome shape matters: a low dome (about 40 cm high) reflects heat onto the pizza. A high dome wastes heat. The oven mouth should be about 30 cm wide and 20 cm high â enough to fit a 12-inch pizza peel. Always build on a solid base like concrete blocks or a stone plinth. Never build directly on the ground. This overview gives you the foundation to choose your oven type. Next, you will learn the science of why wood-fired cooking works.

lessons.title: The Science of Wood-Fired Cooking
lessons.body: Wood-fired cooking works because of three things: high heat, radiant heat, and wood smoke. When you burn dry hardwood like acacia or eucalyptus, the oven floor reaches 400Â°C to 500Â°C. A 12-inch pizza cooks in 90 seconds at this temperature. The heat comes from three directions: the fire on one side, the hot floor below, and the dome above reflecting heat back down. This is called radiant heat. Unlike a gas oven, wood fire also produces smoke that flavors the crust. The key is to keep the fire small and to the side. You want a rolling flame, not a roaring bonfire. Use small pieces of wood, about 30 cm long and 5 cm thick. Hardwoods burn longer and hotter than softwoods like pine. In Africa, acacia, mopane, and eucalyptus are excellent. Avoid treated wood or painted wood â they release toxic fumes. The oven needs to be preheated for 45 to 60 minutes. Start with a small fire, then add wood gradually. The dome should turn white-hot (about 450Â°C). You know it's ready when the soot burns off the dome. For a 12-inch pizza, the floor temperature should be around 350Â°C to 400Â°C. If the floor is too hot, the bottom burns before the top cooks. If too cold, the crust is pale and dry. Use an infrared thermometer to check. You can also throw a pinch of flour on the floor â if it browns in 2 seconds, it's ready. The science also involves moisture. Pizza dough contains water. In a hot oven, that water turns to steam and puffs the crust. That's why you get air pockets. A wood-fired oven with a low dome traps steam better than a tall one. Finally, remember that heat moves from hot to cold. The oven walls absorb heat and release it slowly. That's why you can bake bread after the pizza fire dies. Understanding this science helps you control your oven, not just guess.

lessons.title: Essential Tools and Safety Gear
lessons.body: Before you build or use a wood-fired oven, you need the right tools and safety gear. For construction, you need: a trowel, a spirit level, a rubber mallet, a bucket for mixing mortar, a wheelbarrow, a shovel, and a measuring tape. For cutting bricks, a masonry chisel and a club hammer work, but a angle grinder with a diamond blade is faster. In Africa, you can buy these at hardware stores or borrow from local masons. Safety gear is not optional. You must wear: safety goggles when cutting bricks, heavy leather gloves when handling hot tools or wood, and a dust mask when mixing mortar or sand. For the oven itself, you need a pizza peel (a flat paddle with a long handle) to slide pizzas in and out. A wooden peel is best for putting pizza in; a metal peel is better for turning and removing. You also need a wire brush to clean the floor between pizzas. An infrared thermometer (costs about 20 USD) is essential to check floor temperature. If you cannot afford one, use the flour test: sprinkle a little flour on the floor â if it turns brown in 2 seconds, it's ready. For the fire, you need a small rake or hoe to move embers. A metal bucket for ash is also useful. Never use a plastic bucket for hot ash. For safety around the fire: keep a bucket of sand or water nearby. Never leave the fire unattended. Wear closed shoes, not sandals. Tie back long hair and avoid loose clothing. When lighting the fire, use dry paper or dry grass, not petrol or paraffin â those cause explosions. Store wood in a dry place. If you are building the oven, make sure the base is level and strong. A 12-inch pizza oven can weigh over 200 kg, so the foundation must support that. Finally, teach everyone who uses the oven these safety rules. In many African communities, wood-fired ovens are shared, so safety is a community responsibility.

lessons.title: Site Selection and Foundation Requirements
lessons.body: Choosing the right site for your wood-fired oven is critical. First, pick a spot outdoors with good ventilation. Never build inside a closed room â smoke and carbon monoxide can kill. The site should be at least 3 meters away from walls, trees, or flammable materials. In Africa, consider the wind direction. Build so that smoke blows away from your seating area. If you are in a rainy region, build under a roof or shelter, but leave open sides for airflow. The ground must be level and stable. Do not build on loose sand or soft soil. You need a foundation. For a 12-inch pizza oven, the foundation should be at least 1 meter x 1 meter and 15 cm thick. Dig 20 cm deep, fill with rubble or stones, then pour concrete (1 part cement, 2 parts sand, 3 parts gravel). Let it cure for 3 days. On top of that, build a base of concrete blocks or bricks up to 80 cm high. This height is comfortable for most people. The base must be perfectly level â use a spirit level. If not level, the oven dome will crack. For the oven floor, you need a layer of insulation. Use a 5 cm layer of sand mixed with clay, or better, a 5 cm layer of perlite or vermiculite if available. Then lay firebricks on top. In Africa, firebricks can be found in cities, but in rural areas, use dense clay bricks and cover them with a thin layer of clay slip. The foundation must also support the chimney. A chimney helps draw smoke away. Use a metal pipe or build a brick chimney. The chimney should be at least 1.5 meters tall. Finally, make sure you have easy access to wood and water. Store wood nearby but not touching the oven. If you are building in a market or community center, get permission and make sure the site is safe for children. A good site makes your oven last for years. A bad site leads to cracks, smoke problems, and wasted money.

lessons.title: Understanding Oven Dimensions for 12-Inch Pizzas
lessons.body: A 12-inch pizza is about 30 cm in diameter. Your oven must be bigger than that to allow for turning and airflow. The cooking floor should be at least 60 cm x 60 cm. That gives you 15 cm of space around the pizza. The dome height should be about 40 cm from the floor to the highest point. If the dome is too high, heat escapes and the pizza cooks unevenly. If too low, you cannot fit a pizza peel or turn the pizza. The oven mouth (the opening) should be about 30 cm wide and 20 cm high. This is wide enough to slide a 12-inch pizza in and out. The mouth should be at the same level as the floor. The ratio of mouth height to dome height is important: mouth height should be about half the dome height. So if dome is 40 cm, mouth is 20 cm. This creates a good draw for smoke and heat. The floor should be made of firebricks laid flat. Each firebrick is about 23 cm x 11 cm x 6 cm. You need about 12 to 15 firebricks for a 60 cm x 60 cm floor. If you cannot get firebricks, use dense clay bricks and cover with a 1 cm layer of clay and sand mix. The dome is built from bricks or cob. For a 60 cm floor, the dome diameter at the base is about 70 cm. The walls should be 10 cm thick for good heat retention. The chimney opening should be at the front of the dome, above the mouth. A 10 cm diameter metal pipe works well. The total oven footprint (including walls) is about 90 cm x 90 cm. This fits on a 1 meter x 1 meter base. For a 12-inch pizza, you can bake 2 pizzas at a time if your floor is 60 cm x 60 cm, but leave space between them. Do not overcrowd. The oven should also have a landing (a flat area in front of the mouth) to rest the peel. Make it 30 cm deep. These dimensions are tested and work well in African conditions. Adjust slightly if your bricks are different sizes, but keep the proportions.

lessons.title: Planning Your Build: Timeline and Budget
lessons.body: Building a wood-fired pizza oven for 12-inch pizzas takes about 3 to 5 days of work, spread over a week. Day 1: gather materials and build the foundation. You need cement, sand, gravel, and water. Mix concrete and pour the base. Let it cure for 24 hours. Day 2: build the base walls with concrete blocks or bricks. Use mortar (1 part cement, 4 parts sand). Check level constantly. This takes 4 to 6 hours. Day 3: insulate the base and lay the firebrick floor. Mix clay and sand for insulation. Lay firebricks flat with a thin clay slip. This takes 3 to 4 hours. Day 4: build the dome. This is the slowest part. Use a brick or cob mix. Shape the dome using a sand mound as a guide. Cover with a layer of clay and straw for insulation. This takes 6 to 8 hours. Day 5: build the chimney and let the oven dry. Do not fire it immediately. Let it air-dry for 3 days, then light small fires for 3 days to cure the clay. A full cure takes a week. So total timeline: 1 week of building plus 1 week of curing. Budget: For a basic brick oven, expect to spend 150 to 250 USD. Breakdown: firebricks (if bought) 50 USD, clay bricks 30 USD, cement 20 USD, sand and gravel 15 USD, metal chimney pipe 20 USD, tools (if you don't have them) 50 USD. In rural areas, you can cut costs by making your own clay bricks and using local sand. In cities, firebricks may be expensive, so use dense clay bricks. Labor is free if you do it yourself. If you hire a mason, add 50 to 100 USD. Always buy materials in bulk to save. Plan your build for the dry season to avoid rain. Also, check local regulations â some areas require permits for outdoor fires. Finally, keep a contingency of 20% for unexpected costs. With good planning, you can have a working oven in two weeks and start baking pizzas for family or business.

quiz.q: Which type of wood-fired oven is most common in Africa because of locally available materials?
quiz.explanation: Brick ovens are most common because clay bricks are locally made and cheap.

quiz.q: What is the ideal cooking floor size for a 12-inch pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: A 60 cm x 60 cm floor gives enough space for a 12-inch pizza and turning.

quiz.q: What is the recommended dome height for a 12-inch pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: A 40 cm dome height reflects heat properly onto the pizza.

quiz.q: Which wood is best for firing a wood-fired pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: Acacia is a hardwood that burns hot and long, unlike softwoods or treated wood.

quiz.q: How long should you preheat a wood-fired oven before baking pizza?
quiz.explanation: Preheating for 45 to 60 minutes brings the oven to the required 400-500Â°C.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a low dome in a wood-fired oven?
options: B) To trap steam and reflect heat
C) To make it look nice
quiz.explanation: A low dome traps steam and reflects radiant heat onto the pizza for even cooking.

quiz.q: Which safety gear is essential when cutting bricks?
quiz.explanation: Safety goggles protect eyes from flying brick chips.

quiz.q: What tool is used to slide pizzas in and out of the oven?
quiz.explanation: A pizza peel is a flat paddle designed for moving pizzas.

quiz.q: What is the flour test used for?
options: A) To check if the dough is ready
quiz.explanation: Sprinkling flour on the floor shows if it's hot enough (browns in 2 seconds).

quiz.q: Why should you never use petrol to light a wood-fired oven?
quiz.explanation: Petrol is highly flammable and can cause dangerous explosions.

quiz.q: What is the minimum distance a wood-fired oven should be from walls?
quiz.explanation: At least 3 meters prevents fire hazards and allows smoke to disperse.

quiz.q: What type of foundation is required for a 12-inch pizza oven?
quiz.explanation: A concrete slab at least 15 cm thick supports the oven's weight.

quiz.q: How long should concrete cure before building on it?
quiz.explanation: Concrete needs at least 3 days to cure and gain strength.

quiz.q: What is the recommended height of the oven base?
quiz.explanation: 80 cm is a comfortable working height for most people.

quiz.q: What material is best for insulating under the oven floor?
quiz.explanation: Perlite or vermiculite provides excellent insulation to keep heat in the floor.

quiz.q: What is the ideal oven mouth size for a 12-inch pizza?
options: A) 20 cm wide x 15 cm high
B) 30 cm wide x 20 cm high
C) 40 cm wide x 30 cm high
D) 50 cm wide x 25 cm high
quiz.explanation: A 30 cm x 20 cm mouth fits a 12-inch pizza and maintains proper heat draw.

quiz.q: How many firebricks are needed for a 60 cm x 60 cm floor?
quiz.explanation: Each firebrick is about 23 cm x 11 cm, so 12 to 15 cover the floor.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a landing in front of the oven mouth?
options: B) To rest the pizza peel
quiz.explanation: A landing provides a flat surface to rest the peel while loading pizzas.

quiz.q: How long does it take to build a wood-fired oven from start to finish?
quiz.explanation: Building takes 3-5 days, plus about a week for curing.

quiz.q: What is the approximate budget for a basic brick oven?
quiz.explanation: A basic brick oven costs between 150 and 250 USD depending on material sourcing.

quiz.q: Why should you build the oven during the dry season?
quiz.explanation: Rain can damage clay and mortar before they cure properly.

quiz.q: What is the recommended chimney height?
quiz.explanation: A 1.5-meter chimney ensures good smoke draw.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a safety rule for using a wood-fired oven?
options: A) Keep a bucket of water nearby
quiz.explanation: Closed shoes are required; sandals do not protect feet from hot embers.

quiz.q: What is the correct ratio for mortar used in the base?
quiz.explanation: A 1:4 cement-to-sand mix is standard for block work.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a chimney in a wood-fired oven?
quiz.explanation: The chimney creates a draft that pulls smoke out of the oven.

quiz.q: How can you test if the oven floor is hot enough without a thermometer?
options: A) Touch it with your hand
D) Put a piece of paper
quiz.explanation: Flour browns in 2 seconds when the floor is at the right temperature.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of a wood-fired oven over a gas oven?
options: A) It is cheaper to buy
B) It cooks faster and adds smoke flavor
D) It is easier to clean
quiz.explanation: Wood fire reaches higher heat and imparts a smoky flavor.

quiz.q: What should you do if you cannot find firebricks?
options: B) Use dense clay bricks with a clay slip
quiz.explanation: Dense clay bricks with a clay slip can substitute for firebricks.

quiz.q: Why is it important to level the oven base?
options: A) To make it look good
quiz.explanation: An unlevel base causes stress that can crack the dome.

quiz.q: What is the recommended thickness of the oven dome walls?
quiz.explanation: 10 cm thick walls provide good heat retention without being too heavy.
